artifact: DiDi Mexico residual T3 finance proof

repository.scope: six residual Mexico corridors from the sealed eight-ID DiDi spine

rules_applied: Exact sealed route IDs only; no substitute OD or nearby terminal.
No peak-day annualization, terminal-total allocation, directional doubling/halving, geometry-derived operations, or country-to-city DiDi inference.
Passenger journeys are kept distinct from vehicle movements and cargo.
Published fares are identified as benchmarks rather than realized operator yield.
Null is retained where exact primary evidence is absent.

finance_gate_note: Exactly one of the six rows, ics-aa6ff40d2d Punta Sam–Isla Mujeres, now has exact-route primary annual passenger demand plus an exact-route published adult fare. It can move from all-null L3_locals to a non-null comparable demand/fare record. The other five rows remain null for annual demand; three future-opportunity rows also lack exact current service and fare proof.

sources.title: INFORMACIÓN de transbordadores 2025
sources.publisher: Administración Portuaria Integral de Quintana Roo (APIQROO)
sources.exact_fact: The 2025 table labels passenger ENTRADAS, SALIDAS and TOTAL. Isla Mujeres shows 121,959 entradas and 116,169 salidas, total 238,128 passengers. Punta Sam shows the mirrored 116,169 entradas and 121,959 salidas, total 238,128 passengers. Each endpoint also shows 2,712 total vessel movements and 433,640 cargo units.
sources.units_and_period: passenger one-way crossing journeys, full calendar year 2025; vessel movements and cargo are separately labeled
sources.route_coverage: Punta Sam–Isla Mujeres transbordador corridor, both directions
sources.directionality: Endpoint entradas/salidas are explicitly reported and mirrored. Use one endpoint passenger total, 238,128, without doubling or halving; do not sum the duplicate endpoint totals.

sources.title: Ruta Punta Sam - Isla Mujeres
sources.source_type: current operator route, timetable and tariff page
sources.exact_fact: The page names origin Punta Sam and destination Isla Mujeres, and the reverse direction. It publishes four weekday departures per direction and three departures per direction on Saturday and Sunday. The tariff section says prices are per one-way trip and publishes Pasajero Adulto MXN 290, Pasajero Niño 3 a 9 años MXN 190, Pasajero Adulto Quintanarroense MXN 80, Pasajero Niño Quintanarroense MXN 60, and Pasajero INAPAM MXN 70.
sources.units_and_period: MXN per passenger per one-way trip; live timetable and tariffs with no stated effective date
sources.route_coverage: exact Punta Sam–Isla Mujeres car-ferry route, both directions
sources.fare_nature: published retail tariff benchmark, not realized operator yield
sources.confidence: high for current publication; effective-date history not stated

sources.title: Tarifas
sources.exact_fact: Ultramar publishes adult one-way MXN 290 and round-trip MXN 580 for Cancún Puerto Juárez–Isla Mujeres, and separately publishes the same tourist adult prices for Cancún Playa Tortugas–Isla Mujeres and Cancún Playa Caracol–Isla Mujeres.
sources.units_and_period: MXN per passenger; live page, no stated effective date
sources.route_coverage: multiple distinct Cancún terminals to Isla Mujeres
sources.fare_nature: published retail tariff benchmark, not realized operator yield
sources.limitation: The sealed row ics-03e3853317 names its origin only as 'Ultramar' and has no boarding-point binding. This multi-terminal fare page cannot identify which Cancún terminal the row represents, so no fare is assigned to that ID.
sources.confidence: high for the operator prices; unusable for exact-row allocation

sources.title: Cancún–Isla Mujeres routes and schedules
sources.exact_fact: The page offers Cancún–Isla Mujeres service and presents separately named Cancún terminals, including Puerto Juárez and hotel-zone terminals.
sources.units_and_period: scheduled departures on live booking page
sources.route_coverage: multiple Cancún terminals to Isla Mujeres
sources.limitation: Operator/current-service evidence is not enough to map the sealed origin label 'Ultramar' to one exact terminal without minting or inferring a boarding point.
sources.confidence: high for current operator operation; not exact-row allocable

sources.title: Water Taxi Tickets to Yelapa
sources.exact_fact: The page says public water taxis run daily from Puerto Vallarta, lists Los Muertos Pier departures at 11:00, 11:45, 15:00 and 17:00, return departures from Yelapa at 08:00, 09:30, 12:00 and 16:00, and quotes MXN 550 round trip per person.
sources.units_and_period: MXN per person round trip; current schedule, no effective date
sources.route_coverage: Los Muertos Pier, Puerto Vallarta–Yelapa, both directions
sources.fare_nature: booking-page retail benchmark, not realized operator yield
sources.confidence: medium; current exact-route commercial evidence but not an authority statistic or audited operator annual report

sources.title: Water taxi from Puerto Vallarta to Yelapa
sources.exact_fact: The page says daily departures only from Los Muertos Pier, publishes MXN 550 per person round trip, lists four Puerto Vallarta-to-Yelapa departures and six Yelapa-to-Puerto Vallarta departures, and states 16% federal sales tax is not included.
sources.units_and_period: MXN per passenger round trip plus stated 16% tax; live page, no effective date
sources.route_coverage: Los Muertos Pier, Puerto Vallarta–Yelapa, both directions
sources.fare_nature: published booking benchmark, not realized operator yield

sources.title: Iniciaron trabajos de rehabilitación del muelle de Playa de los Muertos en Puerto Vallarta
sources.exact_fact: The notice says rehabilitation of the Playa de los Muertos pier was undertaken to improve safety and efficiency for tourist-service providers, tourists and maritime-transport users under Jalisco's maritime-connectivity program.
sources.units_and_period: infrastructure/current-use context; no route passenger counts
sources.route_coverage: Los Muertos pier, Puerto Vallarta; not an exact Yelapa demand table
sources.confidence: high for pier/public-use context; no route-level finance value

sources.title: Ley de Navegación y Comercio Marítimos
sources.publisher: Cámara de Diputados del H. Congreso de la Unión
sources.exact_fact: Article 42 states that shipowners engaged in inland navigation and cabotage require a permit from the Secretaría to provide passenger transport and tourist-cruise services; it separately states that passenger transport and nautical tourism with recreational/sport vessels require a port-captain permit.
sources.units_and_period: legal permission requirement, current federal law
sources.route_coverage: Mexico generally; no route-specific permit grant

sources.title: Ciudades donde opera DiDi en México
sources.exact_fact: The official index says DiDi operates in listed Mexican cities and includes Cancún and Puerto Vallarta. It does not identify a DiDi ferry, water-taxi, marine-crossing product, marine operator, or count of marine crossings.
sources.units_and_period: city service-presence page; no marine-network metric
sources.limitation: Cannot prove city-to-island operation, a marine product, a crossing count, or Los Cabos marine operation.
sources.confidence: high for listed road cities; unusable as marine-census evidence
